name: drift
kind: A hidden two-state truth that flips at random times and is reported only through tastes that are sometimes false; the rung's size is the share of false tastes, so the brain must average evidence over several meals while still forgetting fast enough to follow a flip.
source: Restless/volatile bandits and reversal learning with probabilistic feedback (Behrens et al. 2007 volatility learning; Bayesian change-point detection; signal-detection with noisy reinforcers; Kalman-style forgetting versus averaging trade-off in animal learning).

rungs.text: (world (meta (link L7) (q T) (cap Ladder) (group drift)) (let s (int 2)) (told (if (= s 0) P F)) (on tick (if (chance (* TICK 0.0125)) (set s (- 1 s))) (set poison (if (= s 0) P F))) (on meal (if (chance 0.05) (set worth (- worth)))))
rungs.desc: Which colour is poison flips at a random moment (about every 80 s) and each meal's taste is false with chance 0.05. Learn: the colour's current meaning, 1 bit held by a running estimate over the last ~tens of tastes; each taste carries only 0.71 bits about it, so about 1.4 meals per bit; the learner must also hold the flip rate (~1 bit per 80 s) tradeoff between averaging and forgetting.
